common_meaning: The sub-continent where the Chacalli language and culture comes from

Literally 'glorious mountains'
The mountain range separating Chacalli from the rest of its landmass.

Literally 'contract'
A confederacy within Chacalli, and the dominant country.

Literally 'fish town'
One of the cities in Neten Nonotzlalitzli, a fishing hub near the coast

Literally 'banquet hall'
One of the cities in Neten Nonotzlalitzli, and its political center

Literally 'jade stone'
One of the cities in Neten Nonotzlalitzli, a mining town rich in resources

From 'comoco', meaning 'bleat'
A domesticated beast in Chacalli, adept at navigating along difficult terrain

Literally 'Fire Empire'
A small tribal empire, and another country within Chacalli

Literally 'ash mother'
A volcano central to the mountains of Tepetozcah Tenyocan, which has been rumored to be near eruption
A temple in the mountains of Tepetozcah Tenyocan, where it is rumored that the Chalice of Kruka is kept
sand
hill
mountainous

Literally 'sand hill'
A region of the port town of Tochtepec where many of the Neten Nonotzalitzli natives live and work.
A type of boat used for fishing in the shallow parts of the ocean near the shore. It has a wide, flat bottom, similar to a raft.
When used alone, a first person possessive ('my'). As a prefix, a negative modifier ('not-').
goodness

Literally 'most goodness'
best

Literally 'not goodness'
bad
'Political' or having to do with politics
A word describing the place for the previous word or adjective. For instance 'Pilcalio Yatl' means 'Politics Place.'
A word describing the place for the following word or adjective. For instance 'Tlan Yankuk' means 'Place to Cook.'
Cooking. Can be used as a descriptive noun or as a verb.
Shelter. Has implications that it's the type of shelter put up in an act of desperation
Place to keep animals
Stables. Used in Neten Nonotzalitzli to store cocomocos.
Storage, or a place to store things.
Freshness, as a noun concept. Also refers to the general 'fresh' feeling one might feel seeing greens.
A driving concept of nationalism, coined by politicians in Neten Nonotzalitzli.
Similar to 'library,' contains slightly more implications of 'pile of books'
Strength, especially the ability to exert force and protect oneself. Commonly associated with military.
Similar to 'progress,' with an implication of 'rules making.' Often associated with political speeches.
Grass. versions of this word are also used to describe fields, plains, or even mere flat areas.
Similar to 'low,' but also meaning for 'short' when speaking about objects.
Storage, but unilke 'Yotli,' with an implication of it being viewable and long-term, like a museum.
The name of the currency used around here. Gold coins are accepted everywhere, though.
Large sized. Like 'tsinto,' not used to refer to creatures, as opposed to objects.
A marketplace. Also refers to machines with many inputs and outputs.
Green. Has some cultural implications of traitorship which have faded generation by generation into more of intrigue or flirtation.
Tree
Traveler (affectionate), and as the world expands, also means 'businessperson.' Built off of 'Tlalo,' meaning 'store.'
A very casual term meaning 'trade,' but without much seriousness. Like calling a company a 'biz.'
Used broadly to refer to death or its related processes, like funerals, elder care, and the concept of rest.
Store. In olden days, was more of a reference to the part of a house from which someone might sell their livelihoods.
Food products, like what a farm or orchard might produce. Helped contribue to the alternate meaning of 'tlalo.'
Referring to laborers or workers. Tends to come with the implication of simplicity and hard-working determination.
Theater, or place to view spectacles
Wheat
A workshop. The first of these orignated as wheat grain mills, but now it refers more to a broader segment of contraption shops.
Comes from an old folk story about a miner who slept in the mines and turned it into his home. Meaning 'the place that's near home.'
Spiritual significance. If something possesses enough Inali, it's more holy or sacred.
Statue
Woodworking. Parts of this word are used to refer to similar concepts, like lumber, carving, and parts of the tree.
Fruit that grows on trees and doesn't need to be replanted.
Stoneworking. More specific concepts within this craft tend to get their own words.
Similar to 'separate,' but with a specific implication of safety as opposed to loneliness.
Warmth. Usually not associated as much with fire as the natural warmth within caves closer to the earth.
The security of a campfire.
Gathering, or a gathering place.
One of the tribes in the jungle. Tends to be hostile, and focused on food.
One of the tribes in the jungle. Tends to be hostile, and focused on material.
One of the tribes in the jungle. Tends to be hostile, and focused on wealth.
One of the tribes in the jungle. Tends to be peaceful, and focused on food.
One of the tribes in the jungle. Tends to be peaceful, and focused on material.
One of the tribes in the jungle. Tends to be peaceful, and focused on wealth.
Please
Thank you
Where, or used for the concept of location. Asking 'Where is X?' is 'Kampa X?'
When, or used for the concept of timing. Asking 'When is X?' is 'Kenih X?'
Why, or used for the concept of reason. Asking 'Why is X?' is 'Lekah X?'
How, or used for the concept of means. Asking 'How does one X?' is 'Ken X?'
